storyline.label: Efficient Learning
storyline.latest_title: TokenEconomizer: Learning from Experience to Make AI Coding Agents Efficient

prior_narrative.tldr: This is a loose cluster of arXiv papers on cheaper LLM inference, not one event. It opened in late October with diffusion-LM decoding and MoE pruning work, and by Nov 8-12 had block-diffusion drafters inside speculative decoding and diffusion LMs learning when to remask their own output.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Callo (Nov 13) runs speculative decoding on invalidated KV cache so agent requests whose context was edited can start decoding before re-prefill finishes under prefill-decode disaggregation.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: The diffusion-LM work is still paper-stage, but the speculative-decoding side is reaching serving systems: drafters verified by the target, and now speculation over stale KV to hide re-prefill latency in agent sessions.

beats.headline: Metacognitive decoding and Measured Coupling aim to cut dLLM decoding cost
Length extrapolation and multimodal hallucination expose weak spots
Non-diffusion-LM efficiency work shares the thread: pruning, MoE serving, compression and agent overhead
beats.summary: These papers share the efficient-inference theme, not the diffusion-LM method; one is an image-diffusion membership-inference paper matched on the word alone.

beats.headline: Speculative decoding papers chase longer accepted drafts
beats.summary: Two papers a few days apart, D-REAL and REAL Loss, both train the drafter on acceptance length instead of token-level loss.

beats.headline: Block-diffusion drafters enter speculative decoding
beats.summary: D3Tree and DForkTree treat a block-diffusion model as the drafter and work on the draft tree the target verifies.

beats.headline: Block diffusion LMs get their own inference optimizations: DUET sparsity and overlapping block denoising
Diffusion LMs learn when to remask and regenerate their own output
beats.summary: The Nov 12 paper uses hidden states, not token confidence, to decide when and what to revise; its diagnosis is run on Sudoku.

beats.headline: Speculation moves into serving: Callo drafts over invalidated KV for agent sessions
beats.summary: Callo and a Baseten post on the inference efficiency frontier are serving-side additions, not diffusion-LM papers.

open_questions: Do the metacognitive-decoding, Measured Coupling and SpecCTMC speedups hold on independent benchmarks at equal output quality?
Does learned remasking improve accuracy on natural-language or code tasks beyond the Sudoku diagnosis, and at what extra decoding cost?
Does any inference framework or vendor ship diffusion LLM serving with parallel decoding?
Does a block-diffusion drafter with a pruned draft tree beat existing drafters on end-to-end throughput under concurrent serving load?
How often does Callo's speculation over invalidated KV get rejected after heavy context edits, and does it still beat waiting for re-prefill then?
Do D-REAL and REAL Loss report comparable acceptance-length gains on the same drafter and target pairs?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Do not plan serving capacity around diffusion LLMs yet. If agent sessions edit context often, measure how much decode time your stack loses to re-prefill on cache misses before evaluating approaches like Callo.

day_captions.ed7966c78dc36a0b: Adjacent: co-designs pruning and scheduling for MoE inference on memory-constrained edge servers, where moving expert weights dominates.
day_captions.edcf9763d6b958dc: Extends the efficiency push to agents by adapting compute spent and text generated per interaction.
day_captions.1423e77dae0d2a75: Adjacent, image side: a membership inference method for testing whether an image was in a diffusion model's training set.
day_captions.a8a5f23cd8e10643: Adjacent: gradual pruning with sparse adaptation to hold LLM quality at extreme sparsity.
day_captions.581b8a72b6b37583: Training-free fix for repetition and quality loss when continuous diffusion LMs generate longer text.
day_captions.01d6db945cd3f0c2: Adjacent: nested MoE with dynamic mixed-precision quantization to shrink MoE inference cost.
day_captions.473a95cd7c540d1a: Adjacent: prompt compression trained with a hybrid of reinforcement and supervised learning.
day_captions.57b08f9866a26766: Targets hallucination in multimodal discrete diffusion LMs by ordering visual gain during mask prediction.
day_captions.219537f3fa2b3690: Adjacent: distills textual skill memory into a self-evolving agent instead of carrying it as prompts.
day_captions.884381d0dd03d261: Lets a speculative-decoding drafter reconsider its guesses in parallel to raise per-guess acceptance.
day_captions.0491c6de7a511fb5: Measured Coupling: picks which tokens are safe to commit together in parallel decoding instead of assuming mean-field independence.
day_captions.2fb1a0f31494270f: Speculative simulation that preserves the exact output distribution when sampling several tokens in parallel.
day_captions.5fbc35eb022e4033: DUET: sparsifies both attention over the growing prefix and processing of the current block in block diffusion LMs.
day_captions.b1fe6c30c1c550df: D-REAL: trains the drafter on acceptance length directly, with unbiased gradients, instead of token-level objectives.
day_captions.a4e942d0f147f07c: Learns to prune block-diffusion draft trees, since every tree node costs a verification row on the target.
day_captions.0aacbce5f85ac122: Builds fork-aware draft trees from a block-diffusion drafter, following DFlash and DDTree.
day_captions.d9424aebc884a5c5: Drafts at phrase level against a frozen target instead of in the target's own token vocabulary.
day_captions.ca0cd6bcfdb70098: Overlaps denoising blocks to make block diffusion LMs more efficient for latency-critical generation.
day_captions.256bf90ce51f6665: Second drafter loss within a week, after D-REAL, that optimizes expected acceptance length for speculative-decoding drafters.
day_captions.d7a4f91e59e352a3: Adjacent: model-agnostic image cropping and compression to cut vision-language inference cost.
day_captions.e267de687efb45c3: Adjacent: argues delegation in multi-agent deep research only pays off when task allocation and subtask execution are coordinated; not a diffusion-LM paper.
day_captions.679b2c4e802619e6: Adds self-correction to the dLLM line: a learned signal for when to remask and regenerate, after finding token confidence misses errors that hidden states expose.
day_captions.018074f62583197d: Brings speculative decoding into disaggregated serving: decode starts on invalidated KV while agent requests with edited context would otherwise wait for re-prefill.
day_captions.018ac20c79d4eeba: Adjacent, vendor side: a Baseten post on the efficiency frontier of LLM inference, surfaced via Hacker News; not a diffusion-LM item.
